incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: kv-cache memory spike (mistral-gqa) — paging oncall@sophie

sophie (oncall): seeing a big memory delta on `mistral-gqa` serving pool, ~3x baseline over last 10m. Latency SLOs breached on a few routes. Investigating.

dinesh: looking at metrics now — heap RSS + cache entries both increasing. Continuous batching window looks like it spiked to 30ms for a subset of requests (should be ~8ms).

sophie (oncall): any recent deploys to runtime or batching config?

dinesh: no deploys in last hour. Noticed a burst of MQA-style requests with long prompt prefixes from a single customer CID=cust-82. Their traffic has a high prefix reuse but different suffixes — seems to have caused per-request KV growth.

ben: can you paste the `kv_cache.size` and `continuous_batch.dist` graphs?

dinesh: attaching quick snip: ``kv_cache.entries: 1.1M -> 3.2M in 12m; continuous_batch.window_ms p50: 8 -> 28; batch_size p95: 64 -> 192``

carlos (not in thread): (reacts :eyes:)

carla: that's consistent with cache amplification — many unique KV keys created by per-conversation prefixes. If we don't evict, memory balloon.

julia (support): customers reporting timeouts on `mistral-gqa-large` endpoints, two support tickets opened (TKT-1022, TKT-1023). Informing them there's an incident.

sophie (oncall): immediate mitigation ideas: 1) lower continuous batch window to 4ms 2) enable aggressive KV eviction (evict threshold 0.6 -> 0.45) 3) temporarily disable KV caching for `mistral-gqa` 4) scale up pod replicas as short term. Which one is fastest?

dinesh: lower window and eviction are config flips — can push via runtime config; disable KV for model is also a config flip. Scaling is slower but doable. I'd do window+eviction first, then scale if needed.

ben: do we have a safe toggle path? `runtime-config` accepts `continuous_batch.window_ms` and `kv_cache.eviction_threshold` per-model. I can push a hot config with canary to one shard.

sophie (oncall): do it. Can we route new requests for cust-82 to older lower-memory variant (mistral-gqa-compact) as fallback?

dinesh: routing table already has `variant_fallback` routes but cust-82 pinned to `mistral-gqa` via dedicated policy. We can temporarily override via `route-policy: emergency-fallback:cust-82 -> mistral-gqa-compact`. Need product sign-off? This is urgent.

erica: product approves emergency override for user-impacting incidents.

ben: pushing hot config: ``PATCH /runtime/config {"continuous_batch.window_ms":4, "kv_cache.eviction_threshold":0.45} // targeting pool mistral-gqa``

deploy-bot: config rollout started (rollout_id=roll-5723) -> canary shard s-7 first.

dinesh: canary metrics look good after 90s: p95 latency down 18%, cache entries flattening on s-7. Proceeding to roll to remaining shards.

ben: applying route override for cust-82 now. ``POST /routing/override {"customer":"cust-82","to":"mistral-gqa-compact","expires":"+30m"}``

julia (support): told customers TKT-1022/1023 we implemented mitigations and are monitoring.

sophie (oncall): scaling up 2 extra nodes to add headroom while rollout completes.

dinesh: after full rollout (5m) kv_cache.entries stabilized at ~1.4M and continuous batch window p50 back to ~6ms. Memory trending down.

ben: leaving KV caching disabled for `mistral-gqa` for 30m as a precaution (config `kv_cache.enabled=false` applied).

erica: support updated customers, one is still seeing occasional 502s but overall better.

sophie (oncall): summary of mitigations applied: 1) reduced continuous batch window to 4ms 2) tightened eviction threshold to 0.45 3) emergency route override for cust-82 -> compact variant 4) temporarily disabled KV caching for `mistral-gqa` 5) scaled pool +2 nodes.

ben: creating rollforward PR to make window change scope-limited and add a guard: don't allow continuous batch size >128 for `mqa` profiles. Link: https://stash.redwood/PR/4487

dinesh: will follow up with an additional hotfix to KV eviction algorithm to avoid extreme per-prefix allocation (LRU + size-aware cap).

erica: should we page infra for a larger root cause? Looks like customer traffic pattern triggered a worst-case of our cache strategy.

sophie (oncall): yes — mark incident Sev2 for now. I'll start an incident timeline doc and assign a postmortem owner.

julia (support): I'll keep customers updated and consolidate tickets.

ben: deploy-bot: `config rollback` not needed — this is a hot patch; we'll revert `kv_cache.enabled` once safe.

deploy-bot: config rollout complete (rollout_id=roll-5723) at 1819876630.

dinesh: last check: memory down to baseline, no new timeouts for 10m. Recommend keeping changes in place while we run a canary suite for 24h.

sophie (oncall): agreed. Postmortem owner: dinesh. Timeline doc: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/1819876543

erica: adding product and support action items.

julia (support): closing the two tickets as 'monitoring' with notes; will reopen if regression.

sophie (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll hand off to next oncall in 30m. :white_check_mark:
